title: Candidate Experience Lifecycle — Microplan & Interview Simulation (WIP)
content:
Purpose: create a compact, repeatable microplan that improves candidate experience from intro to first-week ramp. This doc bundles: (A) interview simulation day design, (B) simplified rubric for cross-functional panels, (C) a 24-hour fast-start onboarding kit for accepted offers, and (D) quick decision/feedback templates. Status: working draft — looking for ops + hiring managers to sign off on simulation scenarios and 'first 24h' task owners.

Context / Why now:
- We want to shorten time-to-decision without degrading signal.
- Feedback from last quarter: candidates find multi-panel days fragmented; hiring managers want clearer comparators.
- Experiment goal: run a 6-week pilot for IC and SWE-1/2 roles in product infra and solutions-eng.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Candidate NPS >= 8/10 at end of process (surveyed immediately after panel).
- Offer acceptance rate >= baseline + 5pp for pilot roles.
- Time-to-offer median <= 6 days from panel completion.
- Hiring manager satisfaction >= 4/5.

High-level pipeline (micro):
1) Intro screening (30m): recruiter + brief role alignment, logistics for simulation day.
2) Simulation day (3h block or split AM/PM): structured activities below.
3) Panel deep-dive (60m): role-specific technical + behavioral.
4) Decision sync (30m): interviewers debrief in same Slack thread + PUSH decision in 48 hours.
5) Fast-start onboarding (24-hour kit) for accept -> immediate onboarding tasks.

Simulation day design (core differentiator):
- Goal: observe candidates in a lightweight, contextualized exercise that mirrors on-the-job work and cross-team interactions. Avoid contrived puzzles.
- Structure (3 segments):
  A) Context brief (15m): hiring manager gives product/infra vignette (1 pager sent beforehand).
  B) Pair-design / collaboration task (50m): candidate pairs with a rotating interviewer (15–20m each rotation) to design a small feature or troubleshoot an incident. Focus on tradeoffs, communication, and prioritization.
  C) Presentation + Q&A (25m): candidate shares approach, interviewer asks clarifying questions.
  D) Rapid culture fit check (30m): behavioral questions anchored to company values; scenario-based probing about ambiguity, ownership, and collaboration.
- Logistics notes: send 1-pager with vignette 48 hours ahead; ask candidate to bring a short slide or notes but not required. Provide 10mins break after pair-design.

Interview rubric (single-sheet, 1–5 anchors):
- Categories: Role Competence, Problem Framing & Tradeoffs, Communication & Collaboration, Ownership & Bias-to-Action, Learning Agility.
- Scoring guidance (anchor highlights):
  5 — Outstanding: clear, prioritized approach that anticipates constraints, communicates decisions, invites collaborators, and demonstrates measurable impact in past examples.
  3 — Competent: can solve core problems with some prompting; explanations ok but gaps under pressure.
  1 — Insufficient: major gaps in fundamentals or inability to explain tradeoffs.
- Calibration examples (for panel pre-read):
  Role Competence: "Explains a distributed cache invalidation approach and quantifies latency cost" (5) vs "Mentions cache without eviction strategy" (2).
  Communication: "Elicits constraints and restates problem; closes loop on next steps" (5) vs "Monologues with no check for alignment" (2).
- Bias mitigation: every interviewer completes a quick implicit-bias checklist before scoring (checkbox list in UI). If any score differs from median by >1 point, interviewer must add clarifying evidence in comments.

Decision flow & timing:
- Interviewers enter scores within 12 hours. Hiring manager convenes 30m decision sync within 24 hours. Recruiter provides salary band + comp template during sync. Offer goal: 48 hours after panel.
- If panel consensus is unclear, run a 30m follow-up with one technical evaluator only (recorded notes). Avoid multiple extra rounds.

Feedback templates (post-reject / post-offer):
- Quick reject (auto): 2-3 bullet points: "We appreciated X; for this role we needed stronger Y." Keep warm for future roles.
- Detailed feedback (opt-in): schedule 20m with recruiter within 5 business days.

24-hour fast-start onboarding kit (for accepted offers):
- Purpose: reduce friction on Day 1 and signal continuity. Kit delivered immediately after signed offer. Includes:
  - Pre-day checklist (account provisioning request link; template to request laptop asset if remote).
  - First-day agenda (team intro + 1:1 with manager + setup hour + orientation): sample calendar.
  - Slack channels to join: #pod-<name>, #onboarding-announce, #help-ops.
  - Small first-task: "read product vignette" + make a 30-minute doc with 3 quick improvement ideas (low cognitive load).
  - Buddy assignment: short note from assigned buddy with calendar invite for first 3 days.
  - Security & compliance pre-reads and a 1-click KMS access request form.
- Owners and SLAs:
  - IT provisioning ticket created by recruiter within 2 hours of signed offer (owner: IT-ops).
  - Manager schedules 1:1 + onboarding slot within 12 hours (owner: hiring manager).
  - Buddy reaches out with welcome note within 6 hours (owner: buddy).

Templates (snippets to paste):
- Offer send note: "Welcome aboard! Attached is your signed offer. Next steps: complete the onboarding kit and expect IT to provision accounts within 24h. Your manager, <name>, will schedule a 1:1 for Day 1."
- Rejection note: "Thank you for interviewing. We enjoyed your discussion on <topic>. At this time we are moving forward with candidates who demonstrated stronger <skill>. We will keep your details on file and welcome future conversations."

Operational checklist for pilot (quick TODOs):
- Recruiter: create candidate intake form with vignette link (due: next Tuesday).
- Hiring manager: finalize 1-pager vignette and sample rubric anchors (due: +4 days).
- IT: confirm provisioning template and asset pool for fast-start (due: +7 days).
- People Ops: prepare NPS survey (2 questions) to send at panel end.
- Interviewers: mandatory 30m calibration session before pilot start.

Open questions / discussion points: (notes-to-self)
- Compensation cadence: how to ensure offers delivered in 48h given payroll approvals for senior hires? Need escalation path.
- Simulation fairness: do we give accommodations (extra time) for candidates with disabilities? Yes — formalize accommodation flow under People Ops.
- Panel length: some hiring managers prefer 2-hour condensed block vs split; test both formats in pilot.

Appendix (calibration anchors & mini-cheats):
- Mini-cheat for interviewers: ask one "scope" question early and one "edge-case" question. Record evidence sentence for each category.
- Quick scorecard template (copy-paste into interview notes): 5 categories x score 1–5 + 3-line evidence field per category + recommendation checkbox (strong, consider, pass).

Links & refs (for pilot pack):
- Confluence baseline: https://confluence.redwood/team-hiring/candidate-lifecycle-2026
- Slack channel for pilot coordination: #pilot-hiring-sim-2026
- Jira: HR-1423 (pilot project)

Next steps (this week):
- Circulate this doc to hiring managers for infra & solutions-eng.
- Book 30m calibration slot with listed interviewers.
- Recruiter to validate asset pool in IT.

Final note: this is intentionally lightweight — the product of many existing heavy playbooks condensed into a micro-experiment. We care about signal, speed, and candidate dignity. Feedback welcome — add comments inline or ping me (Sofia).

Unresolved: add templated interview accommodation request flow, decide whether to record pair-design sessions (privacy concerns), and finalize compensation approval SLA.
